# AuthKit for Java — AI Agent Integration Guide

## What This Is
Self-hosted Spring Boot 3.x authentication backend consumed by this frontend.
Default dev backend: `http://localhost:8083`
API base: `/api/v1`

## Quick Setup (Backend)
1. Clone backend repository.
2. Configure datasource, JWT/refresh-cookie settings, mail/OTP settings, and allowed frontend origin.
3. Run backend (typically on port `8083`).
4. Frontend should set `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8083` (frontend normalizes to `/api/v1`).

## Authentication Flow
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login`  
  Request: `{ email, password }`  
  Response: `{ accessToken, user }`
- `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` (uses HttpOnly refresh cookie)  
  Response: `{ accessToken, user }`
- `POST /api/v1/auth/logout`  
  Response: `204 No Content`

## Registration Flow (3 Steps)
1. `POST /api/v1/auth/signup/request` with `{ email }` to send OTP.
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/signup/verifyotp` with `{ email, otp }` to receive a short-lived signup token.
3. `POST /api/v1/auth/signup/verifytoken` with `{ email, token, password }` to complete signup.

## Forgot Password Flow (3 Steps)
1. `POST /api/v1/auth/forget/email` with `{ email }` to send OTP.
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/forget/otp` with `{ email, otp }` to verify OTP and get reset token.
3. `POST /api/v1/auth/forget/reset` with `{ email, token, newPassword }` to reset password.

## User & Session Endpoints
- `PUT /api/v1/user/password` with `{ currentPassword, newPassword }`
- `GET /api/v1/user/sessions`
- `DELETE /api/v1/user/sessions/{jti}` (revoke one session)
- `DELETE /api/v1/user/sessions` (revoke all other sessions)
- `DELETE /api/v1/user/me` (self account deletion)

## Admin Endpoints
- `GET /api/v1/admin/users`
- `DELETE /api/v1/root/delete/{userId}`

## Frontend Integration Rules
- Store access token **in memory only** (React/provider state), not `localStorage`.
- Refresh token stays in secure HttpOnly cookie (`withCredentials: true`).
- On `401`: call `/auth/refresh`, retry original request once, clear session and redirect to login if refresh fails.
- Preserve original protected route and return user there after successful login.

## OAuth2 Redirect Handling
After OAuth provider callback, frontend lands at `/oauth2/redirect/` and calls `/auth/refresh` to hydrate app session from cookie.

## Error Shape
Backend error payload is expected as:
`{ status, error, message, path, timestamp }`
